title.narrative: Proactive Response and Early Planning for Action to Reinforce Emergency-Readiness (PREPARE)

description.narrative:
Note:This project has been shifted from Start Ready Risk Pool 4 to 5: SB Hub Allocation and extended until 30 April 2027, based on the confirmation. Noakhali District is highly disaster-prone, facing frequent cyclones, tidal surges, floods, tornadoes, riverbank erosion, and droughts. Recent heavy rains and upstream water flow have caused severe flooding, damaging homes, infrastructure, and livelihoods. Past cyclones (Sidr, Aila, Amphan) have triggered major humanitarian crises. Women, children, the elderly, persons with disabilities, and marginalized groups are disproportionately affected. Proposed Locations:
Companiganj: Char Elahi, Musapur
Hatiya: Char Ishwar, Char King, Hatiya Paurashava, Harni
Subarnachar: Char Clerk, Mohammadpur
Union selection is based on needs assessments, contingency planning, and coordination with the Start Fund Network to avoid duplication. Project Approach:Christian Aid will use an inclusive, equitable, and community-centered approach, prioritizing:
People in extreme poverty
Persons with disabilities and elderly people
Women, adolescents, pregnant/lactating mothers
Marginalized and ethnic minority communities
Women migrant workers
Key Outputs:
Vulnerable communities adopt early measures to protect lives and assets.
Enhanced community and institutional capacity to reduce cyclone risk.
Early Action Activities:
Inception & Staff Orientation – Sessions on safeguarding, inclusion, AAP, gender, and compliance.
Early Warning Dissemination – Via miking and community outreach, covering evacuation, shelter, and safety guidance.
Repair Works (9 schemes) – Embankments and access roads near shelters to ensure safe evacuation.
Health Kits at 16 Shelters – Pre-positioned kits with ORS, sanitary napkins, soap, and first aid.
Solar System Repairs – Ensure lighting in shelters to reduce GBV risks and increase safety.
Dry Food for 3,300 HHs – In Char Elahi, Musapur, Char Clerk, and Mohammadpur. Kits include flattened rice,biscuits, ORS, and more to meet food needs for 3 days. Due to remoteness and lead time, Hatiya upazila was excluded from dry food distribution.
MPCG for 3,300 HHs – Unconditional cash transfers (aligned with Cash Working Group standards) to support urgent needs including transport, food, medicine, and minor shelter repairs.
PDM – Conducted using Start Fund tools to assess relevance, use, and community feedback.
A strong Complaint and Feedback Response Mechanism (CFRM) will be active throughout to ensure community voices are addressed and integrated.Tentative Targeted Households by Union:
